methods.name: BRC error linearization / Pell-Pade tail transport
capabilities: exact affine post-truncation derivative ratio (1+x)E^(n+1)/E^n=1/2-n
exact recursive BRC gap orbit with second difference -2 and third difference 0
exact integer Pell-Pade lower approximant to sqrt((m+h)/m) for h=1,2
second-order linear recurrence in Pade order X_(n+2)=(4m+2h)X_(n+1)-h^2 X_n
sqrt-free Pell norm identity (m+h)B_n^2-mA_n^2=h^(2n+1)
exact integer <=2-correction certificate J h^(2n+1)<=m A_n B_n
certified table-free BRC root/remainder transport
methods.core_law: For E_K=sqrt(1+x)-1-P_K, derivatives above order K satisfy (1+x)E_K^(n+1)/E_K^n=1/2-n, while ordinary BRC correction gaps satisfy G_q=G_0-q(2a+q). The diagonal Pade/Pell approximant obtained from (1+sqrt(1+x))^(2n+1)=P_n+sqrt(1+x)Q_n yields homogenized integers A_n,B_n with (m+h)B_n^2-mA_n^2=h^(2n+1). This makes A_n/B_n a rigorous lower sqrt-ratio predictor and gives the exact sufficient certificate J h^(2n+1)<=m A_n B_n for at most two BRC basin corrections.
methods.hard_boundary: Classical Pade/Pell approximation is prior art. The current contribution is exact BRC composition, certification, and error-linearization bookkeeping. The Python reference path is substantially faster than the previous high-order Taylor table-free tail but still slower than direct optimized isqrt on isolated steps. No asymptotic factorization speedup, RSA-practicality, optimal multiplier order, or Foundation promotion is claimed.

methods.name: BRC prioritized direct multiplier jump / 2-adic irredundant scan
capabilities: exact elimination of odd-N multipliers m congruent 2 or 6 mod 8 as impossible difference-of-squares targets
exact reduction of every successful immediate witness at m congruent 4 mod 8 to the smaller multiplier m/4 with the same gcd factor
scan-complete odd-N static multiplier representative residues {0,1,3,5,7} mod 8
exact N-visible repeated m->m/4 reduction when the already-known BRC ceiling root is even
exact impossibility diagnosis when dynamic reduction lands in a 2 mod 4 target or a 4 mod 8 target with odd reduced ceiling root
state-level gap-test irredundancy readout without changing the static candidate set
same-parity multiplier factor-pair structural scoring on the exact representative set
direct exact BRC transport from the retained m=1 root/remainder state to arbitrary target m<=100
proved at-most-11 odd-basin corrections for direct jumps
methods.core_law: For odd N, m congruent 2 or 6 mod 8 is impossible as a difference of squares. If 4 divides m and an immediate ceiling-square witness has even ceiling root x, then its gap root is even and dividing x,y,m by 2,2,4 gives the same immediate witness and gcd factor at m/4; this may be repeated using the halved ceiling root. The static special case m=4*l with l odd therefore makes every 4 mod 8 multiplier redundant and leaves residues {0,1,3,5,7} mod 8 scan-complete. For target t<=100 the retained m=1 BRC state reaches t exactly with at most 11 odd-basin corrections.
methods.hard_boundary: Difference-of-squares feasibility, static scan irredundancy, and state-dependent gap-test irredundancy are distinct. The static/dynamic 2-adic reductions and direct jump are exact; the same-parity factor-pair ranking is only a finite empirically useful heuristic and is not claimed optimal. Retained 0 mod 8 states with odd ceiling root can be genuine first hits, so that class cannot be uniformly deleted. Multiplier-Fermat/Hart/Lehman remains classical prior art. No global novelty priority, asymptotic factorization speedup, theorem about semiprime ratio distributions, or Foundation promotion is claimed.

methods.name: BRC pairwise multiplier root/remainder transport
capabilities: exact integer root/remainder transport between arbitrary source and target multipliers <=100
one-sided lower predictor with exact odd-basin correction
safe correction bound ceil(sqrt(t/m))+1, hence <=11 globally and <=2 for downward jumps
exact nonmonotone structural-priority state stream with one initial N-dependent root
cached source-target dyadic scale constants with no new checked-in predictor payload
explicit negative audit for simple N-modular/root/remainder/phase adaptive routing shadows
methods.core_law: Given mN=J^2+R and beta=sqrt(t/m), A=floor(2^B beta), q=floor(AJ/2^B) is a lower target-root candidate with sqrt(tN)-q < beta+3/2. Therefore at most ceil(beta)+1 BRC odd-width crossings recover floor(sqrt(tN)); G=tN-q^2 is computed exactly as R+(t-m)N-(q-J)(2J+q-J), valid for both upward and downward multiplier moves.
methods.hard_boundary: Finite exact multiplier<=100 reference surface. Pairwise scale constants are cached runtime data. The simple N-dependent shadow features tested in the accompanying note are finite negative evidence only, not an independence theorem. Difference-of-squares/multiplier-Fermat/Lehman mathematics remains classical; no optimal multiplier order, asymptotic factorization speedup, or Foundation promotion is claimed.

methods.name: BRC phase quotient/remainder transport
capabilities: exact five-phase transport of divmod(2*h*J,4*m+h) on the common order-one deep tail
two direct seed divmods per mod-8 source phase followed by recurrence-only quotient generation
proved phase second-difference bounds -3..51 for h=1 and -3..99 for h=2
exact product-free residual recurrence using retained roots, quotients and division remainders
512-entry 10-bit normalized lower reciprocal table with 1024-byte logical raw payload
proved non-negative correction estimate within at most one plus one exact comparison
optional large-integer backend that composes with the order-one linear BRC tail and staged square-gap cascade
methods.core_law: For one fixed mod-8 phase, S_h(m)=2h*sqrt(mN)/(4m+h) has 0<=Delta_8^2 S_h<=48h on 4m^5>=N. Since q_h=floor(2h*floor(sqrt(mN))/(4m+h)) differs from S_h by less than 2, its exact integer second difference is in [-3,51] for h=1 and [-3,99] for h=2. With X_i=q_i D_i+r_i and D_(i+1)=D_i+32, the residual relative to qhat=2q_i-q_(i-1) is rho=2h(J_(i+1)-2J_i+J_(i-1))+2r_i-r_(i-1)+64(q_(i-1)-q_i), so the next quotient/remainder follows from only a bounded correction. A 10-bit upper-bucket reciprocal seed estimates each non-negative correction from below within one.
methods.hard_boundary: Exact only on the already-certified common order-one deep tail and increasing odd-N mod-8 representative stream. Native big-integer division remains faster in the measured 1024/2048-bit Python cohorts; the tracker is an optional large-integer long-stream backend with a runtime-dependent crossover. It does not reduce the multiplier horizon, alter factorization complexity, or imply RSA practicality.

methods.name: BRC priority vertical scheduler / remainder-aware arbitrary-jump certificate
capabilities: exact arbitrary a->b multiplier jump through a retained remainder lower coordinate with at most one BRC basin correction for 1<=a,b<=100
compute the admissible monotone horizontal state family once and consume it in an arbitrary declared vertical-search order
priority-ordered vertical factor search preserving the same full finite multiplier x t rectangle
explicit ascending-order latency baseline
finite cross-scale priority-rank and runtime audit
methods.core_law: If aN=J^2+R and sqrt(aN)=J+delta, then L=J+R/(2J+1) satisfies sqrt(aN)-L=delta(1-delta)/(2J+1). With beta=sqrt(b/a)<=10 and two extra dyadic predictor bits over the existing <=100 multiplier bound, floor(sqrt(bN)) differs from the lower dyadic prediction by at most one. For the default performance path, however, the complete monotone horizontal BRC state family is materialized once and only the expensive vertical-wheel evaluation is permuted by the experimental multiplier priority; this permutation preserves the declared finite rectangle exactly.
methods.hard_boundary: The current nu(m)^4/m priority is experimental and not a theorem. The arbitrary one-correction jump is exact but was slower than direct CPython isqrt on tested 10-state priority prefixes, so it is not the default fast path. Multiplier-Fermat/Lehman/Hart search and residue wheels remain classical prior art. Finite rank and timing gains do not imply asymptotic factoring improvement or Foundation promotion.

methods.name: Critical BRC word, primitive-orbit and Euler-prefix arithmetic
capabilities: exact total and based-closed critical dominant branch-word counts from integer K
exact primitive periodic-orbit counts by Mobius inversion
exact determinant-zeta reciprocal coefficients
exact truncated primitive-orbit Euler-product coefficients with determinant cross-check
verified finite prefix bundling of total/closed/primitive/zeta data
methods.core_law: For the canonical integer critical-degeneracy matrix K, T_n=tr(K^n)=sum_{d|n}dP_d and 1/det(I-zK)=product_n(1-z^n)^(-P_n); all data are exact rational-gauge invariants because K itself is gauge invariant.
methods.hard_boundary: Primitive periodic edge-word orbits are not WBRC-T29 simple feedback-support circuits and P_n are not arithmetic prime counts. Classical dynamical-zeta/entropy structure only; no runtime orbit-enumeration speedup, Shannon-probability or infinite-state claim.
